audit.note: Independent re-audit after repair cycle 1 (American English and editorial depth), against quality-contract §B and a sentence-by-sentence comparison with the pre-repair record. American English: no behaviour, artefact, judgement or other British forms remain (behavior, artifact, judgment). Prose only, four paragraphs; no positional or time-sensitive words; pronouns resolve (the 'which' after 'running system' refers to the system; 'the gap' refers to the inclusion gap just described). Earlier audit repairs all survive: the definition keeps 'or in every case up to a stated limit'; carry-over is still limited to a property each behavior must satisfy, such as an invariant; the bound example is still 'values drawn from a small range'; the reentrancy example still uses a contract that holds deposits. Depth changes checked: (1) The bounded-to-unbounded argument now gives only 'such as an inductive step'; dropping 'or a proof that the limit is large enough' loses no condition, because the general requirement (an additional argument that nothing beyond the limit behaves differently) remains, and sufficient depths and cutoff results are explained in Model Checking. (2) The sentence associating model checking with bounded and theorem proving with unbounded results was parent repetition: Formal Methods' comparison already gives model checking 'every state of a bounded model / nothing beyond the model's bounds' and theorem proving 'properties established without bounds'; its removal also takes away the 'commonly' hedge, but with the claim gone no overclaim remains, and the record now names neither sibling. (3) Assumption examples cut from three to two (honest majority of validators; collision-free hash function); 'messages delivered within a known delay' was illustrative only, and the axiom/precondition/environment-constraint forms remain. (4) New clause 'or a value outside the range' is correct and completes the parallel with the three listed limits. (5) 'with respect to the property' tightens a phrasing the previous audit called loose; the claim is now precise. Other condensations (the satisfaction sentence, 'its result is a statement about that limit', 'so its statement carries no such qualifier', 'valid, and silent about theft', the tool-defect sentence) keep every claim. No new inaccuracy or overclaim found. Splits: FV ~ Model Checking holds; no exploration, temporal logic, state explosion or trace reading; the general statement of what a bounded pass is worth stays at the level of any bounded technique, while Model Checking gives configuration and depth bounds, k-induction, IC3 and cutoffs. FV ~ Theorem Proving holds; no kernels, tactics, lemmas or proof cost; 'not the semantics the tool reasoned with' states FV's gap, while Theorem Proving explains how a semantics enters a proof. Formal Specifications is only the artifact verified against; the supply-conservation example shows the specification as trusted, not how it is checked against intent. Depth outcome: 818 to 770 words; the cuts are parent repetition, material a sibling explains, and one illustrative example. Density remarks (not defects): the bounded paragraph's examples (steps, participants, range) parallel Model Checking's fourth node, channel capacity and counter range at a more general level, which fits FV's claim on result strength; the trusted-base enumeration repeated in the closing sentence is how that sentence makes its point; little further removable material remains.

audit.note: Independent re-audit after repair cycle 1 (American English, FV split, Model Checking / Formal Specifications boundary, editorial-depth pass), compared sentence by sentence with the pre-repair record at the single leaf placement (Formal Methods / Model Checking). American English: the two British forms ('behaviours', 'behaviour') are now 'behaviors'/'behavior'; no other British spellings; prose only (seven paragraphs, matching the prose design); no positional or time-sensitive words. FS boundary applied: the operator-by-operator explanation of LTL and CTL and the illustrative property statements ('no two nodes decide different values', 'each submitted request is eventually answered') are removed; temporal logic is now named as the language the search checks (LTL checked against each execution, CTL against the branching structure of the state graph), and safety and liveness appear only as shapes of search and counterexample (finite violating execution: search reachable states for a bad one or finite paths for a violating prefix; infinite violating execution: reachable cycle, product with a violation automaton, restriction to fair cycles; trace ending in the violating state versus lasso). The claim 'how a model checker explores a state space against properties stated in temporal logic' is still explained: the record says what the search does with each kind of property. Formal Specifications (authored) owns what properties state, their environment assumptions and the prohibition/obligation/ordering classes; Model Checking restates none of it. FV split held: FV owns what verification establishes, the model-versus-system gap, the trusted base and bounded-versus-unbounded strength in general (including the failure asymmetry and that a bounded pass needs an extra argument); Model Checking keeps only model-checking-specific mechanics: configuration versus depth bounds and what a completed search of a bounded configuration covers, BMC unrolling, and the concrete mechanisms (reachability diameter with over-estimates, k-induction, IC3/PDR, cutoffs) behind FV's 'additional argument', without restating that one is needed. Theorem proving, symbolic execution and static analysis are not explained. Nothing technically necessary lost and every earlier hedge kept: fairness (now 'restrict that search to fair cycles, excluding those in which a process that stays ready to act is never scheduled'; the dropped clause that many models fail liveness only through starvation survives in the lasso sentence that a starving loop points to a missing fairness constraint rather than a design flaw; the 'ask whether a fair schedule allows the loop' wording is compressed into that consequence); lasso traces intact; abstraction keeps the over-approximation condition for preserved passes of universal properties, spurious counterexamples and CEGAR; symmetry reduction keeps 'up to' the factor and the soundness condition with the lowest-identifier counterexample; bounded configuration versus depth intact (one illustration dropped, the channel holding three messages at capacity two, which is redundant with the fourth node and counter wrap and with channel capacity in the bounding list); diameter now stated directly with its reason ('since every reachable state then lies within it') and over-estimates; k-induction unchanged; IC3/PDR unchanged; cutoffs keep their conditionality ('for models meeting the conditions of a particular class of protocol'). Safety search is slightly more exact than before ('or the finite paths through them for a violating prefix'). The pronoun 'drive it through' is now 'drive the implementation through', removing an ambiguity. No new inaccuracy, overclaim or contradiction found; section B items 1-12 checked. Depth outcome: 1245 to 1152 words, all removals are FS-owned exposition, redundant illustrations or connective compression. Density remarks (not defects): the bounding list in the containment paragraph partly anticipates the configuration examples of the pass paragraph; 'This is state explosion: the space can grow exponentially' lightly restates the multiplication it names; 'that tools or engineers then shorten' could go. None repeats parent or sibling territory.

audit.note: Independent re-audit after repair cycle 1, compared sentence by sentence with the pre-repair record and read against the Formal Methods parent and the authored Formal Verification, Model Checking and Formal Specifications records. American English: 'generalised' is now 'generalized', 'modelled' is now 'modeled', and 'judgement' is now 'judgment'; no British forms remain. Retained conditions and hedges: 'as long as the kernel checks what it produces'; only reconstruction keeps an external solver out of what must be trusted; the parser and code generator lie outside the kernel's check 'unless they have been verified in turn'; 'some' kernels rechecked or verified; 'many' assistants report axioms and placeholders; the reviewer's reading list is still the report, the statement and the definitions it uses. Requested tightenings are present: automatic inference 'succeeds only for restricted classes of invariant', and parametric participants extend the result to 'configurations of any size', which matches FV's wording. The undecidability clause now comes before 'so no procedure finds them in general', which makes the causal order explicit. Pronoun fixes: 'If the semantics treats' (was 'it'), 'those functions' (was 'those') and 'The check does not establish' (was 'It'). Depth pass: 1177 to 1150 words. Removed: the opening sentence about what the assistant works over, which is folded into the engineer's first step; the filler 'The effort shows in the size of the result'; 'relative to the tactics and automation around it' (the remaining 'kept small so that it can be inspected' is still accurate); and 'When automation calls'. The wrong-model and parametric-size sentences give the prover-side mechanism behind FV's gap and coverage points. Density remarks (not defects): 'Some semantics are written to be executable ... conformance tests' and the solver-only verifiers contrast are the most removable sentences left, though each adds a distinction tied to the kernel or the semantics. The topic sentence 'To prove anything about code, the prover needs the code inside its logic' could merge into the next. No signals.

audit.note: Independent re-audit, repair cycle 1, against quality-contract B at both placements (Formal Methods and Protocol Specification), compared sentence by sentence with the pre-cycle record. Finding across both repairs: the first repair's sentence made finality itself conditional ('a finalized block stays final only while enough validators follow the protocol'), false as a necessary condition; the second repair moved the condition onto the guarantee ('a finalized block is guaranteed to stay final only while enough validators follow the protocol'), which is correct (with more than a third of stake faulty, conflicting finalization becomes possible, so the guarantee lapses, not finality as such) and consistent with the paragraph's close, 'the protocol has those properties whenever the assumptions hold', and with its opening that whether the properties hold depends on the environment; the 'enough validators' clause matches the later 'more than two thirds of the stake' assumption. FV duplication: the sentence 'a guarantee quoted without them claims more than was specified' is removed; FV's 'a claim that a system is formally verified is incomplete until it names ... under which assumptions' now stands alone, while the specification-side point (a specification states its properties together with what they assume, and the assumptions are part of its meaning) is kept. MC boundary: temporal properties stay on the specification side as what a specification states: safety properties as prohibitions at every point (orderings included, correctly, since a violated ordering shows in a finite prefix), liveness properties as eventual obligations, temporal-logic formulas and abstract state machines named as forms, refinement stated in one clause; nothing on search, finite versus infinite counterexamples, lasso traces, fairness, specific logics or exploration, which Model Checking owns. Naming safety and liveness is a classification of specified properties, not their checking. Earlier audit corrections retained: postconditions 'can' refer to old values; assumptions attach to the protocol's properties generally, not to obligations alone; an unreachable event makes trivial only properties about what holds whenever it occurs. Nothing technically necessary lost: the dropped 'a specification written as code is precise about what it computes', 'described in terms the tool understands', the duplicate 'no account balance is negative' invariant example (the example survives in paragraph one) and 'from documentation' (now 'partly from the code itself') are redundant or implied. Accuracy spot checks: self-transfer postcondition unsatisfiable for a nonzero amount; do-nothing implementation meets a safety-only specification when its initial state violates none of them; 'repairs tend toward the silent direction' is supported by the reason given. Pronouns checked ('they' = properties in paragraph five; 'they'/'it' = specification and model / the event in paragraph eight): clear. American English throughout (behaviour corrected to behavior). Prose only, placement-neutral, true at both placements; parents say nothing about it, so no duplication. Depth: 1252 to 1201 words, 8 paragraphs; density improved by merging the precondition and code-as-specification sentences, tightening paragraph four into safety/liveness/forms and paragraph seven's authorship sentence, without losing a claim component. Remark: 'so nothing prompts a second look' is slightly broader than the earlier 'nothing in the check', but in context it describes the passing check and the next paragraph supplies the human review, so accepted.

'Abstract state machine' is named as one form a protocol specification takes, with a one-clause gloss of its role there; state machines as a concept are not explained. Named, not explained.

The sentence names temporal-logic formulas as the form a specification's temporal properties take; Model Checking's sentence names which logics and how each is checked. Shared vocabulary at the boundary, specification side only; not a defect.

No change needed.

groupAudit.note: Group re-audit after repair cycle 1, all six members read side by side. Splits hold. FV/MC: FV gives the general coverage argument (bounded check vs unbounded proof, asymmetric failures, a bounded pass needs an added argument such as an inductive step, coverage is not trust). MC gives the mechanism behind it: a complete search in a bounded configuration covers executions of any length in that configuration but no larger one, a depth bound leaves out more, and completeness thresholds, k-induction, IC3 and cutoffs are its own routes past a bound. The two agree, and FV dropping 'a proof that the limit is large enough' and its sentence linking MC and TP to the two kinds of result loses nothing another member relies on: MC carries the depth threshold concretely, and the parent's comparison relates the families. FV/TP: FV lists the trusted base in general (specification, model, tools, assumptions, vacuity from contradictory assumptions). TP owns how a kernel shrinks the tool part, how a semantics is accepted as a definition, and how environments enter as hypotheses. TP's called contract that may call back is the remedy for FV's reentrancy example, and its witness environment answers FV's vacuity, so the two complement each other without restating. MC/FS after the boundary decision: MC names LTL and CTL (linear vs branching) and treats safety and liveness only as search and counterexample shapes (finite violating prefix, fair-cycle search, lasso trace). FS owns what properties state: safety as prohibitions at every point including orderings, liveness as eventual obligations, an abstract state machine as a specification, and environment assumptions as part of the meaning. The definitions agree, and neither repeats the other. No member now explains individual temporal operators. With no temporal-logic concept in the map, that is an accepted consequence of the boundary, not a gap a member owns: FS's 'at every point' and 'eventually' carry what the group needs. FS no longer says that a guarantee quoted without its assumptions claims too much. Its assumption paragraph now states only what the specification means. SE/MC: SE's bounding (loop unrolling, path caps, time, search order deciding reach) and MC's bounding (processes, channel capacity, value range, depth, plus BMC unrolling) are each their own mechanism. SE's point that paths outnumber states contrasts implicitly with MC's stored-state search, and merging states differs from symbolic state sets. SA/SE/FV on soundness and silence: SA defines sound as over-approximation (silence means no modeled execution errs) and flags the opposite bug-finding usage. SE describes itself as under-approximating without overloading 'sound'. MC's 'reduction is sound' (does not hide behavior) and TP's soundness of a semantics for the running code both fit SA's primary sense and FV's inclusion condition, so there is no contradiction. What silence means is stated once per method, in that method's terms (SE: explored paths under the checks made; SA: kinds checked under its language model; FV: inconclusive runs establish nothing). The shared thread, that a method checks only what is stated, appears as one method-specific clause each in FV, SE and SA, while FS owns the full argument (wrong or incomplete specifications, error direction, validation against intent). FV's total-supply/theft sentence is the minimal illustration its trusted-base claim needs, against FS's frame-condition treatment. Terms are consistent across members: model (formal representation, including a language semantics), specification vs property (a specification states properties), bound, safety, liveness. Repetition: openings are the six definitions, phrased differently, and the second paragraphs open differently. MC and SE share an arc (mechanism, explosion, mitigations, results, limits of a pass), but that arc is their planned claims and each fills it with its own mechanism. SA, TP, FV and FS follow different arcs. Several members close on what their result does not establish, which is the substance of their claims, not a cloned cadence. Examples draw on the domain's stock situations (balances, transfers, reentry, consensus decisions), each tied to a different mechanism. All six are prose by recorded design decisions, and the group has no signal. American English is clean. No group-level defect, and nothing is reopened.
